newsitem.title: USA: Explosion at Clark Illinois refinery, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Explosion at Clark Illinois refinery, no injuries.

text.p: An explosion early Saturday rocked a Clark Refining & Marketing Inc. refinery in south suburban Chicago but no one was injured, a company spokesman said.
The explosion occurred at about 6 A.M. CDT/7 A.M. EDT when propane gas apparently ignited at the Blue Island, Illinois refinery, said Clark spokesman Syd Wiley.

"As far as we know at this point in time, we had a release of propane ... and something ignited," Wiley said in a telephone interview, adding that the company did not know how the propane had been released.
The propane pipe was shut off at either end and the fire, in about a 20-foot radius, burned itself out in about 90 minutes, Wiley said.
That section of the refinery will be shut down until it is repaired, Wiley said. He did not know how long this would take.
Federal and state industrial safety officals have been notified of the fire, Wiley said.
In March 1995, a fire and explosion at the refiney killed two workers, Wiley said. Later that year, a discharge of hydroflouric acid caused part of the plant to be shutdown temporarily.
"This is completely unrelated to past mishaps," Wiley said of Saturday's explosion.
Clark refining is a subsidiary of Clark USA Inc.
